messages:
maria: Heads up — after bringing up model X on Redwood and running the eval suite we see consistent token-count shifts vs HF tokenizer that change perplexities. Small example: 'ﬁ' ligature becomes two tokens on conversion. anyone seen this with the hf->redwood conversion?
kevin: can you paste the exact tokenizer config.json you used to convert? sounds like a normalization difference (NFKC vs NFC/NFD).
maria: pasted below — we used the normal hf export + our convert script:```json
{
  "model_max_length": 2048,
  "tokenizer_class": "ByteLevelBPETokenizer",
  "add_prefix_space": false,
  "normalizer": {"type": "NFKC"},
  "pre_tokenizer": {"type": "byte_fallback"}
}```
ashley: quick note: HF tokenizer repo historically had subtle pre-tokenizer ordering — some models applied normalization before byte-fallback, others after. If Redwood's loader applies byte fallback first it will change where combining marks end up.
samir: can you show raw token ids for a case that regresses? e.g. the ligature -> tokens diff. also include the serialized vocab/merges.
maria: sample input and tokens:```text
input: "office ﬁle"
hf.tokens: [502, 13, 78]  // single token for 'ﬁ'
redwood.tokens: [502, 12, 34, 78]  // split into two tokens around fallback
redwood.conv-log: "normalizer=NFC, pretoken=binary_fallback_then_split"
```
kevin: that log is telling — convert script must have fallen back to NFC. Did you run convert with --preserve-normalizer? our converter has a flag to force keep_hf_normalizer (we default to a legacy flow).
maria: i tried converting with default CLI (`redwood-convert model_dir/`) — didn't see a warn. is there a recommended CLI flag?
ashley: use `--keep-normalizer` or set env REDWOOD_CONVERT_KEEP_NORMALIZER=1. Also check `--pretokenizer-order=hf` if you want HF's exact ordering.
samir: we should add a unit that loads a small HF tokenizer, converts it, and asserts tokenization roundtrip for a canned set (ligatures, nonspacing marks, ZWJ combos, CJK spaces). i'll draft a PR.
ci-bot: build #6421 passed for redwood/convert on main.
maria: i ran quick repro with `pip install tokenizers==0.13.2` and explicit normalizer:```py
from tokenizers import Tokenizer
from tokenizers.normalizers import NFKC

T = Tokenizer.from_file('tokenizer.json')
T.normalizer = NFKC()  # matches HF export
print(T.encode('office ﬁle').ids)
```
kevin: hmm if HF exported NFKC and our convert step coerced to NFC somewhere (maybe due to python stdlib call) then quantized model downstream will see different prefix caching and KV shapes — that could explain perf differences during batching too.
ashley: also check special tokens mapping — if pretokenizer changes split points, offsets for <|user|> style tokens might shift. I've seen evals fail because chat template separators moved into the previous token.
maria: action items: 1) samir to open PR adding roundtrip tests + add a conversion flag to preserve ordering, 2) kevin to scan convert logs to detect normalizer coercion, 3) i'll re-run evals on a pinned build with `--keep-normalizer`.
samir: PR link when ready: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4567 (WIP) — adding tokenization roundtrip tests + sample artifacts.
kevin: small workaround for now: run `python -c "import unicodedata; print(unicodedata.normalize('NFKC', s))"` on training/eval corpora before tokenizing to match what our converted tokenizer currently does. ugly but quick. :grimacing:
maria: noted. i'll re-run the quant experiments with both flows and post diffs. if it reproduces we'll gate the dedicated rollout until we either preserve HF normalizer or document the conversion change.
ashley: and let's add a short note in model-onboarding checklist: check normalizer type, pretokenizer ordering, and a small token-level regression test.
ci-bot: deploy job for pr/4567 started — will post status. :rocket:
maria: thanks all — posting results shortly.
